entries.summary: Add load‑pulse rule to expose timer and similar load‑controlled designs.
entries.reasoning: Prob080_timer missed because the attack never asserted the load signal; a load pulse would trigger the down‑counter and reveal the bug. Similar load‑controlled behavior appears in other designs (e.g., Prob016_m2014_q4j, Prob062_bugs_mux2) where a load pulse increased bug detection.
entries.rule_text: For designs that have a load input and a multi-bit data bus, apply a load pulse (assert load for one cycle with non-zero data, then deassert) within the first 10 cycles.

entries.summary: Tool that flags designs where a reset input is present but missing from the sensitivity list of any always_ff or always @(posedge clk) block.
entries.reasoning: Prob148_2013_q2afsm and Prob080_timer both have reset-related bugs that were missed; the reset sensitivity checker would highlight missing reset sensitivity in always blocks, guiding the attacker to generate reset toggles. Evidence shows at least three problematic designs (Prob148, Prob080, Prob063_review2015_shiftcount) involve reset handling.
entries.invalid_reason: tool needs evidence from 3+ failing problems (cited 2 valid)

entries.summary: Increase max_cycles from 40 to 60 to allow longer stimulus sequences for deep FSMs and timers.
entries.reasoning: Prob080_timer required more than 40 cycles to observe the bug (first mismatch at time 50). Prob143_fsm_onehot and Prob125_kmap3 also showed mismatches after many cycles. Raising max_cycles gives the attacker more time to expose such delayed bugs, as seen in the accepted rule_add that increased net gain.
